what_its_for: Risperidone is used to treat certain mental health conditions including schizophrenia, bipolar disorder (manic episodes), and irritability related to autism. It helps balance certain chemicals in your brain to reduce symptoms like hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), delusions (false beliefs), mood swings, and aggressive behavior.
how_to_take: Take risperidone exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take the tablet or liquid form by mouth with or without food. Swallow tablets whole — do not crush or chew them. If you are using the liquid (oral solution), measure your dose carefully using the dropper provided. You may mix the liquid with water, coffee, orange juice, or low-fat milk, but do NOT mix it with cola or tea. If you are using orally disintegrating tablets (ODT), place the tablet on your tongue and let it dissolve — do not chew it. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: Your dose will be set by your doctor based on your condition, age, weight, and how you respond to the medication. Do not change your dose or stop taking it without talking to your doctor first. Stopping suddenly can cause your symptoms to come back or cause withdrawal effects. Adults with schizophrenia usually start at a low dose (around 2 mg per day) and the doctor may slowly increase it. Your doctor will find the lowest dose that works best for you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store risperidone tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the liquid (oral solution) at room temperature and use it within 3 months of opening the bottle. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush medications down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of unused medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking risperidone — it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can cause drowsiness. Avoid getting overheated or dehydrated — be careful in hot weather, during exercise, and when taking hot baths or saunas, as risperidone can affect your body's ability to regulate temperature. Avoid taking other medications (including over-the-counter drugs or supplements) without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as many drugs can interact with risperidone.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: uncontrollable movements of your face, tongue, or body (this could be a sign of a serious condition called tardive dyskinesia); high fever, stiff muscles, confusion, or irregular heartbeat (signs of a rare but serious condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome or NMS); fainting or feeling like your heart is racing or skipping beats; trouble swallowing; signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst, frequent urination, or blurred vision; thoughts of harming yourself or worsening depression; swelling of your hands, feet, or face; or a painful erection that will not go away (in males). Also contact your doctor if your symptoms are not improving or are getting worse.
when_it_works: Risperidone does not work immediately. You may start to notice some improvement in sleep, agitation, or anxiety within the first few days. However, it may take 1 to 2 weeks or longer to see improvement in hallucinations, delusions, or mood symptoms. Full benefits may take 4 to 6 weeks or more. It is very important to keep taking your medication every day, even if you feel better, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Elderly patients with dementia: Risperidone is NOT approved for treating behavioral problems in elderly patients with dementia and carries a serious warning (called a Black Box Warning) because it may increase the risk of stroke and death in this group. Children and teenagers: Risperidone can be used in children for certain conditions (such as autism-related irritability starting at age 5, and schizophrenia or bipolar disorder starting at age 10 or 13), but doses are lower and the child will need regular monitoring for weight gain and growth. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Taking risperidone during the third trimester of pregnancy may cause the baby to have temporary withdrawal symptoms after birth. Your doctor will help you weigh the risks and benefits. Patients with kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to start you on a lower dose and increase it more slowly.
